method: grep -rilI over research/repos, .git and documents/ excluded; ambiguous names re-run with -w (word boundary) and the hits read for context
finding: The open-source corpus does NOT substantially name the commercial legal-SaaS ecosystem. It is dominated by free public court data (PACER, CourtListener). Commercial vendor names either do not appear, or appear as false positives.

false_positives_confirmed.ironclad: matches the case name 'Kenai Ironclad v. CP Marine Services' in juriscraper PACER test fixtures, not the CLM vendor
false_positives_confirmed.clio: 4 word-boundary hits: a province name in lexpredict-lexnlp address data, a PACER docket HTML fixture, and one genuine product reference in lawve-ai/awesome-legal-skills billable-time SKILL.md

consequence: The competitor product list in research/answers/D-systems-and-tools.md is category knowledge, NOT corpus-grounded. Confirming or mocking those surfaces requires each vendor's published API documentation as a separate evidence source; the repo corpus cannot supply it.
